04f7df2540a10358e8cee2430d256fdf1ede781c.caption: Diagram of the token syntax with three column groups: Namespace (system, i.e. name, acronym; (theme), i.e. subbrand; (domain), i.e. web, app), Type (category, i.e. background, content, border; property, i.e. spacing; concept, i.e. feedback, interaction) and Modifiers (variant, i.e. primary, dynamic; state, i.e. hover, disabled; scale, i.e. numbers, t-shirt sizes; mode, i.e. ondark, onorange). The legend marks basic parts as bold, optional parts in parentheses and parts not relevant for spacing as greyed out, so category, concept, state and mode are greyed. Below, the example token $ds-subbrand-web-spacing-dynamic-m is annotated: system is ds, theme is subbrand, domain is web, property is spacing, variant is dynamic and scale is m.

0fc3ca765fcd3aba76a8f09639045ad1c95faa74.caption: Two rows, each with a desktop wireframe and a narrow mobile wireframe, and a legend at the right: Core Tokens (Static spacings) in purple labelled "Core Spacing" and Semantic Tokens (Dynamic spacings) in teal labelled "Dynamic Spacing". Callout 1: two images with captions side by side separated by a vertical teal gutter labelled spacing-dynamic-xs (24px) on desktop, which becomes a horizontal teal gap labelled spacing-dynamic-xs (16px) between the stacked images on mobile. Callout 2: an image next to a text block separated by a vertical teal gutter labelled spacing-dynamic-xs (24px) on desktop, while on mobile the stacked image and text are separated by a purple gap labelled spacing-24 (24px), a static core token.

A purple overlay marks the large core spacing (spacing-32 to spacing-160) between the second entry and the button.

Callout 1: the Figma variable picker listing spacing-160 (160), margin (16) and the spacing-dynamic variables xs (16), s (24, selected), m (32), l (40) and xl (56), next to the Auto layout panel with direction gap 16 and padding fields 24 and 32. The spacings are overlaid and labelled, for example spacing-dynamic-xl, spacing-dynamic-xs, spacing-24 and spacing-16; the page is a single column at S, with side-by-side modules, four-column card rows and footer columns on the wider breakpoints.
